rows.description: A teenager or adult believes that avoiding eye contact or fidgeting proves lying. Research shows such cues are weak, since nervous truth-tellers and calm liars are both common.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult trusts people who are charming, similar or attractive, and doubts those who seem awkward. Warmth is a poor test of honesty, and fraudsters use it on purpose.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: affection, embarrassment, doubt, trust

rows.description: An adult verifies claims through consistent details, documents and independent sources rather than trusting a gut feeling about sincerity. Fluent, confident storytelling can be a sign of practice as much as of truth.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A mature person keeps trust as a default but raises the standard of proof when stakes are high. This avoids both naive belief and paranoid accusation.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager showers a teacher or older student with compliments to win favour or marks. The praise is aimed at an outcome, not at the person.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Learning to tell warmth from steering [Response]
rows.description: A teenager learns that a friend who praises and also disagrees is more trustworthy than one who only praises. Honest friends are pleasant, and they do not need something in return.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A person receiving lavish praise from someone who wants something feels warm and less critical. Flattery works by making disagreement feel rude.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Spotting the ask behind the praise [Observer]
rows.description: A colleague notices that compliments arrive right before a request or a favour. Sincere praise is specific and does not depend on a yes.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A wise person accepts a kind word, waits before deciding, and judges the request on its merits. Praise is enjoyed, and decisions are kept separate from it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A person floods a new partner or friend with attention, gifts and promises of forever within days. It can come from real loneliness or from a wish to secure control, and the intensity is the warning sign.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: affection, loneliness, overwhelm, trust
